description: The semantic stage decides this rule too, and by the same reasoning the runtime uses: a handler block is not a procedure body, so `return` and `stop` inside one are outside any procedure even when the `every`/`on_click` sits inside a `define` (spec/execution-model.md:657-660, spec/error-model.md:116,119). Both codes are asserted in one program because the checker reports every occurrence, which the executing fixtures cannot do — execution stops at the first error. Added at the logic/spec reviewer's request during review round 3, which found the corpus had no `check: true` fixture carrying a `stop` inside a handler block at all: measured, the four that mention `stop` (`check/stop-outside-proc`, `check/stop-in-comprehension`, `check/control-flow-in-procedure-clean`, `heritage/check/a-genuinely-unmatched-delimiter-is-still-reported`) place it at the top level, in a comprehension, or inside a procedure body.
